'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****The [[Taliban]] enters [[Lashkargah]], the provincial capital of [[Helmand Province]], capturing large areas of the city, according to a provincial [[government of Afghanistan|government]] spokesman, who reported heavy fighting between government forces and the [[Islamist]] group as civilians flee the city. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-conflict/taliban-fighters-enter-provincial-capital-clash-with-afghan-forces-idUSKBN2F01U2 (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Gulf of Oman incident]]
**A [[Romania|Romanian]] [[Captain (naval)|captain]] and a [[United Kingdom|British]] [[bodyguard]] are killed in a [[Loitering munition|suicide drone]] attack on a [[Liberia]]n-flagged [[Japan]]ese-owned [[oil tanker]], belonging to an [[Israel|Israeli]] company, near the coast of [[Oman]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/30/ship-operated-israeli-billionaire-company-attacked-off-oman (Al Jazeera)]
*Two supporters of the [[Zambia]]n political-leading party [[Patriotic Front (Zambia)|Patriotic Front]] are stabbed to death by supporters of the opposition party National Development in the capital [[Lusaka]], amid an increasing tension over the [[2021 Zambian general election|imminent elections]]. Four people are arrested. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/1/zambia-deploys-army-to-curb-violence-ahead-of-elections (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] imposes a two-week [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in eight [[Provinces of Cambodia|province]]s bordering [[Thailand]] as well as a nationwide night curfew in an effort to reduce the resurgence of [[COVID-19]] cases caused by the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/cambodia-locks-down-thailand-border-areas-over-delta-variant-fears/2317895 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] begins the world's first third-dose vaccination campaign for people over 60 years old, with [[President of Israel|president]] [[Isaac Herzog]] and his wife Michal receiving a third dose of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-s-president-gets-third-covid-vaccine-dose-kicking-off-world-s-first-campaign-1.10057111 (''Haaretz'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]]ese [[Minister of Health, Labour, and Welfare|health minister]] [[Norihisa Tamura]] says that the country has entered an "extremely frightening" stage of the pandemic as the number of cases increases in [[Tokyo]]. The [[Government of Japan|government]] also extends the state of emergency in the capital and expands it to three [[Greater Tokyo Area|surrounding prefecture]]s and the city of [[Osaka]] from August 2 to August 31. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58024158 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines]]
****The [[National Capital Region]] will be placed under the strictest [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines|Enhanced Community Quarantine]] (ECQ) in an effort to reduce the resurgence of COVID-19 cases caused by the Delta variant. The ECQ will be in effect from August 6 to August 20. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/07/30/21/metro-manila-ecq-from-august-2021 (ABS-CBN News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record 8,649 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 137,062. [https://en.vietnamplus.vn/3657-cases-added-to-vietnams-covid19-tally-on-july-30-evening/205582.vnp (Vietnam Plus)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Fourth Merkel cabinet|Angela Merkel's cabinet]] approves a plan to require travellers over the age of 12 who have not been vaccinated or recovered from COVID-19 to show a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test result]] regardless of whether they are travelling by airplane, car or train. People travelling to [[Germany]] from "virus variant areas" will also require a negative test result, even if they have been vaccinated or have recovered from COVID-19. These rules will be in effect beginning on August 1. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-germany-tightens-entry-rules-for-unvaccinated-travelers/a-58706824 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Moscow]] abolishes a widely-flouted requirement for people to wear gloves on public transport and in shops and other public places as the number of COVID-19 cases declines. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/moscow-cancels-glove-wearing-requirement-covid-19-situation-improves-2021-07-30/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya]]
****[[Kenya]] bans all public gatherings and in-person meetings, as well as extends the nationwide curfe] to from 10:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m., in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2021/7/30/kenya-bans-in-person-meetings-public-gatherings-as-covid-surges (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda]]
****[[Uganda]]n [[President of Uganda|president]] [[Yoweri Museveni]] eases its second nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] that allow some business hubs, private and public transport to reopen and operated with restricted capacity limits due to drop of positivity rate of COVID-19 in the country. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-07-30/uganda-relaxes-lockdown-to-ease-economic-fallout-from-pandemic (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****The [[United States]] surpasses 100,000 daily reported cases for the first time since February 11. [https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2021/us/covid-cases.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Cuban protests]]
**The United States places sanctions on the [[Policía Nacional Revolucionaria|Cuban police force]] and two of its police leaders. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/07/30/treasury-slaps-sanctions-on-cuban-police-force-and-its-leaders-over-crackdown-on-protests.html (CNBC)]
*[[Philippines–United States relations]]
**[[President of the Philippines|Philippine president]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] suspends the termination process of the [[Philippines–United States Visiting Forces Agreement|Visiting Forces Agreement]], a military pact between the Philippines and the United States. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-aims-shore-up-philippine-ties-troop-pact-future-lingers-2021-07-29/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**Twenty-four-year-old Tong Ying-kit is sentenced to nine years in prison after being convicted last week for [[vehicle ramming attack|driving his motorcycle]] into three riot police last year. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/hong-kong-man-sentenced-9-years-prison-first-national-security-case-2021-07-30/ (Reuters)]
**Police arrest a 40-year-old man at a mall for booing the [[Chinese national anthem]] during the ceremony for [[Hong Kong]]'s first gold medal at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]]. Police added that the man also carried a Hong Kong colonial flag and that he was arrested on grounds of the man's aim to "incite hatred and politicize sports". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/hong-kong-investigates-china-anthem-booing-during-olympics-broadcast-mall-2021-07-30/ (Reuters)]
*[[Immigration detention in Australia]]
**An [[Iran]]ian [[Kurd]]ish [[asylum seeker]] living among the community in [[Australia]] sues the [[Australian Government|Commonwealth government]] in the [[Federal Court of Australia|Federal Court]] for detaining him in two hotel rooms for over a year. This is the latest in a growing movement of [[refugee]]s suing Australia for alleged [[human rights in Australia|human rights]] abuses. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jul/30/kurdish-refugee-sues-australian-government-for-alleged-unlawful-imprisonment-in-melbourne-hotels (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**The [[European Court of Justice]] confirms the lifting of parliamentary immunity of MEPs and Catalan independence leaders [[Carles Puigdemont]], [[Toni Comín]] and [[Clara Ponsatí]], thereby allowing Spanish courts to prosecute and extradite them to Spain. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/07/30/carles-puigdemont-loses-appeal-against-loss-of-mep-immunity (Euronews)]
*[[Western Togoland]]
**Charles Komi Kudzordzi, leader of the Home Study Group Foundation, is arrested by [[Ghanaian Armed Forces|Ghanaian national security officials]] for declaring parts of the [[Volta Region]] independent in 2019. [https://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Western-Togoland-founder-Papavi-arrested-after-months-of-hiding-1319953 (GhanaWeb)]
